governanceNotes: D1 batch 27 (2026-09-23): one bounded post-amputation phantom-pain association authored per-identity under the ME-30/ME-31/ME-33 amputation-family precedent (arm, foot, hand, leg, and ankle disarticulation each carry their own level-appropriate phantom-limb edge); this identity had been deferred in ME-31/ME-32 only pending credible targets and carries no negative disposition.

The veterans upper-limb survey anchor reports transradial and transhumeral levels specifically; elbow disarticulation is a distinct level not separately stratified in that survey, so the level-proximity extrapolation is recorded as a guard on the edge.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: In a national survey of 776 veterans with major upper-limb amputation, 73% reported phantom limb pain with mean intensity 4.2/10, and 42% reported daily-to-always PLP frequency, with higher-level amputations showing higher odds of any PLP (transhumeral OR 1.76, shoulder OR 3.78 versus transradial; Balakhanlou 2021); the nationwide 3,374-amputee survey independently characterizes PLP prevalence and phenomenology across amputation levels (Diers 2022).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR 3.310 is established by this association evidence: population prevalence does not establish an individual nexus without documentation of the amputation, the phantom pain syndrome, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review; the survey's level odds cover transradial, transhumeral, and shoulder strata rather than elbow disarticulation specifically, and residual-limb pain, neuroma, and prosthetic factors can coexist with or mimic phantom pain.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized transection-reorganization pathway: elbow-disarticulation nerve transection interrupts afferent input from the missing forearm and hand, and the resulting dorsal-horn sensitization and cortical reorganization are hypothesized to generate phantom sensation and pain perceived in the absent limb segments; the level-odds gradient in the veterans survey is consistent with more proximal transection carrying greater phantom-pain burden, but the individual pathway must be established from pain characterization, amputation records, and specialist evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The evidence documents high PLP prevalence after upper-limb amputation generally and a proximal-level gradient, but elbow disarticulation as a specific level was not separately stratified in the cited surveys; phantom pain must be distinguished from residual-limb and neuroma pain, pre-amputation pain and neuropathy must be assessed, and the individual relationship requires case-specific review; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of the elbow disarticulation (level, cause, date); documented phantom limb pain by validated assessment with chronology; distinction of phantom pain from residual-limb and neuroma pain; assessment of pre-amputation pain, peripheral neuropathy, and cervical pathology; prosthetic-fit and use review; specialist assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Residual limb pain, neuroma, or poorly fitting prosthesis as the pain generator
Peripheral neuropathy or cervical spinal cord pathology
Pre-amputation or phantom memory pain of independent etiology
Complex regional pain syndrome of the residual limb
Spinal cord injury or psychiatric contributions to post-amputation pain

evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of the elbow disarticulation (level, cause, date); documented phantom limb pain by validated assessment with chronology; distinction of phantom pain from residual-limb and neuroma pain; assessment of pre-amputation pain, peripheral neuropathy, and cervical pathology; prosthetic-fit and use review; specialist assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: phantom limb pain is documented in 73% of a national upper-limb amputee cohort with a proximal-level gradient consistent with elbow disarticulation, but population prevalence does not establish an individual nexus and the specific level was not separately stratified; no causation is asserted.

sourceReferences.citation: Balakhanlou E, Webster J, Borgia M, Resnik L. Frequency and Severity of Phantom Limb Pain in Veterans with Major Upper Limb Amputation: Results of a National Survey. PM R. 2021 Aug;13(8):827-835. PMID 32896094.
